rich_summary: This section recounts the controversial death of the great teacher Drona during the Kurukshetra war and the fury it awakens in his son, Aswatthaman. Suspecting deceit, Drona asks whether his son is dead. Torn between truth and the need for victory, Yudhishthira ambiguously declares that “Aswatthaman” is slain—referring to an elephant but muttering the qualifier so softly that Drona believes his son dead. Grief-stricken, Drona lays down his weapons and enters meditation on the battlefield. Despite protests from warriors and Arjuna’s plea to spare their teacher, Dhrishtadyumna beheads the defenseless preceptor. When Aswatthaman hears of this, he erupts in grief and rage, condemning the deceit and swearing vengeance on the Panchalas and Yudhishthira. The episode highlights the moral breakdown of the war and sets the stage for Aswatthaman’s devastating retaliation.

highlight_spans.why: Yudhishthira’s fateful half-truth about 'Aswatthaman'—the deceptive moment that breaks Drona’s will to fight.
Drona’s grief and vulnerability leading to his death, culminating in Dhrishtadyumna seizing and beheading the unarmed teacher despite protests.
Dhritarashtra’s long praise of Aswatthaman’s power and character, foreshadowing the terrible force his vengeance may unleash.
Aswatthaman’s furious response to his father’s humiliation and death, especially his anguish over Drona’s hair being seized.

top_scenes.scene_text: The aged warrior Drona sits in meditation on the battlefield after hearing of his son’s death while Dhrishtadyumna rushes forward with sword raised as other warriors shout for him to stop.
Dhrishtadyumna gripping Drona’s hair with one hand and striking off the preceptor’s head as shocked warriors and Arjuna rush forward too late.
Aswatthaman standing in the battlefield with blazing red eyes and clenched fists, breathing like a serpent as rage ignites within him after hearing of his father’s death.
